'''Marie-Odile Soyer-Gobillard''' (born 9 April 1939) is a French biologist, [[Doctor of Science]], Honorary Emeritus Director of Research at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS) and President of an association dedicated to scientific research.

At the [[Observatoire océanologique de Banyuls-sur-Mer|Arago Laboratory]], her scientific work, recognized worldwide, focused on the cellular and molecular study of protists, in particular [[dinoflagellate]]s. She formed and led a cell and molecular biology team, which supported her scientific activity. She has progressively introduced the most advanced techniques for the study of marine cell biology.

Over the past ten years, she has become known to the general public for her studies on psychiatric disorders in children exposed ''in utero'' to synthetic hormones, in particular [[diethylstilbestrol]] (DES), as well as on their multigenerational effect.<ref>{{cite web |title=Resilience: a scientist's campaign against synthetic hormones – Marie-Odile Soyer-Gobillard's testimonial |url=https://www.des-is-it.org/public/en/news/post/resilience-a-scientist-s-campaign-against-synthetic-hormones-marie-odile-soyer-gobillard-s-testimonial |website=DES is it |language=en}}</ref> This work is carried out in close collaboration with the association Hhorages-France of which she is the President.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Perturbateurs endocriniens, hormones de synthèse : tous exposés, tous concernés - 16 octobre 2019 |url=https://www.obs-banyuls.fr/fr/partager/les-mercredis-de-la-connaissance/conferences-2019/156-perturbateurs-endocriniens-hormones-de-synthese-16-octobre-2019.html |access-date=2022-05-08 |website=Observatoire océanologique de Banyuls-sur-Mer}}</ref>

== Career ==
In September 1961, at 22, after obtaining a Graduate Degree ([[:fr:Diplôme d'études supérieures en France|Diplôme d'études supérieures]]), she joined the CNRS at the [[Observatoire océanologique de Banyuls-sur-Mer]] (OOB), a marine laboratory, known as the "Laboratoire Arago", where she spent her entire career.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marie-Odile SOYER-GOBILLARD |url=https://ref-france.typepad.fr/refinternational/2013/02/marie-odile-soyer-gobillard.html |access-date=2022-05-08 |website=Association ReF-International-Méthode SOLÈRE®}}</ref>

In 1974, she founded the Cell and Molecular Biology Department, dedicated to the study of the mechanisms that control the functioning of certain marine organisms used as models by researchers on, among other things, the structure of chromosomes, the proteins of the mitotic apparatus and the course of the [[cell-cycle]].

From 1980 to 1989, she was an elected member of the Board of Directors of the Arago Laboratory. From 1987 to 1991, she was an appointed member of the National Committee of the CNRS (section 28, Biology of Organisms) of which she was vice-president. From 1975 until her retirement in 2000, she was in charge of a research group, of the Electron Microscopy Service as well as of the Cell and Molecular Biology Department until 1995<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2021-02-01 |title=Protistology and Cell Biology at the Marine Arago Laboratory of Banyuls-sur-Mer (1961–2000): Personal Recollections |url=https://hal.sorbonne-universite.fr/hal-03128970/file/PROOFS%20PROTIS_125792.pdf |journal=Protist |language=en |volume=172 |issue=1 |article-number=125792 |doi=10.1016/j.protis.2021.125792 |issn=1434-4610 |access-date=2022-05-08|doi-access=free |last1=Soyer-Gobillard |first1=Marie-Odile |pmid=33607482 }}</ref>

== Work ==
=== Scientific papers ===
To date, Marie-Odile Soyer-Gobillard has published more than 180 publications in international peer-reviewed scientific journals, particularly in cell and molecular biology, and has given more than 200 presentations at conferences.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marie-odile Soyer-gobillard - Academia.edu |url=https://independent.academia.edu/MarieodileSoyergobillard |access-date=2022-06-02 |website=independent.academia.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Recherche - Archive ouverte HAL |url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/search/index/?q=*&authFullName_s=Marie-Odile+Soyer-Gobillard |access-date=2022-06-02 |website=hal.archives-ouvertes.fr |language=fr}}</ref>

=== Selected books ===
* Margulis L., M.O. Soyer-Gobillard & J. Corliss, Evolutionary protistology. The organism as cell. Rep. ''Origins of Life'', 1984, 13 (3-4). D.Reidel Publishing Company, Dordrecht/Boston, 183 pp ({{ISBN|9789027717658}}).
* Soyer-Gobillard, M.O. & Schrevel, J, The Discoveries and Artistic Talents of Édouard Chatton and André Lwoff, Famous Biologists. (Bilingual version, French-English). Cambridge Scholars Publishing (CSP) Editor, June 2020. (283 pp., 123 Figs) ({{ISBN|978-1-5275-5066-7}}).
* Testimonial (in French): ''Une résilience ou les trois Marie-Odile'', Nombre 7 Editions, 2021 ({{ISBN|9782381536606}})
*Resilience: A scientist's campaign against synthetic hormones.  Nombre 7 Editions, collection Hippocrate, 2022, 416 pp. ISBN 978-2-38351-211-0

=== Artwork ===
In October 1998, after the death of her son, she started working with clay in a workshop in [[Perpignan]]. In 2000, she became a sculptor and held her first exhibition in [[Banyuls-sur-Mer]], the homeland of [[Aristide Maillol]]. In 2013, she declares "''I had lived the ignoble, and I wanted to recreate beauty''".<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=36,9° - Implants, prothèses, lentilles: gros soucis! - Distilbène: un héritage empoisonné - Play RTS |url=https://www.rts.ch/play/tv/369/video/implants-protheses-lentilles-gros-soucis-distilbene-un-heritage-empoisonne?urn=urn:rts:video:3965550 |access-date=2022-05-08 |language=fr}}</ref>

Her work has been exhibited on numerous occasions, notably in Paris, Perpignan, Barcelona and Sézanne. In September 2000, she received the 3rd international prize of Sculpture at the International Art Fair of [[Argelès-sur-Mer|Argèles-sur-Mer]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marie Odile GOBILLARD-SOYER - Artcadémie |url=http://artcademie.free.fr/artistes/MOGS.htm |access-date=2022-05-09 |website=artcademie.free.fr}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
* In 1974, Marie-Odile Soyer-Gobillard received the Paul Wintrebert Foundation Prize<ref name=":7">{{Cite book |last=Schrevel |first=Joseph |title=The discoveries and artistic talents of Édouard Chatton and André Lwoff, famous biologists. |date=2020 |isbn=978-1-5275-5554-9 |oclc=1178633254 }}</ref>
* In 1988, she received the Trégouboff Prize of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (quadrennial marine biology prize).<ref name=":7" />
* From 2000 to 2005, she was Emeritus Research Director at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]].<ref name=":7" />
* From 2004 to 2009, she was a corresponding member of the [[National Museum of Natural History, France|National Museum of Natural History]] (MNHN) of Paris.<ref name=":7" />
* On July 14, 2021, on the occasion of the [[Bastille Day]], she was appointed [[Legion of Honour|Chevalier de la Légion d'Honneur]], in recognition of her scientific and associative career.<ref>{{cite web |title=Perpignan : Marie-Odile Soyer-Gobillard reçoit officiellement la médaille de chevalier de la Légion d'honneur |url=https://www.lindependant.fr/2021/09/26/perpignan-marie-odile-soyer-gobillard-recoit-officiellement-la-medaille-de-chevalier-de-la-legion-dhonneur-9814410.php |website=L'Indépendant |language=fr}}</ref>
